title: U.S. House · Ohio's 10th District
area: Southwest Ohio, including Dayton and Montgomery County.

context.text: Incumbent Michael Turner (R) advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Kristina Knickerbocker won the Democratic primary. Thomas McMasters won the Libertarian primary.

summary.text: Michael Turner is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 10th Congressional District, which he has represented since 2003. He is a former chairman of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and previously served as mayor of Dayton.

background.text: Born in Dayton, Ohio; graduated from Belmont High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio Northern University.
Served as mayor of Dayton before his election to Congress.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the House Committee on Armed Services, including its Strategic Forces and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 118th Congress (2023-2024), after serving as its ranking member in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Kristina Knickerbocker is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 10th Congressional District. She is a family nurse practitioner and U.S. Air Force veteran.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2015 to 2025.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Azusa Pacific University (2014) and a graduate degree from The Ohio State University (2022); works as a family nurse practitioner.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will protect Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP and the Affordable Care Act and support a public option.
positions.quote: I’ll protect Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP, and the Affordable Care Act; support a public option to lower premiums and expand care

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will repeal harmful tariffs that raise prices.
positions.quote: repeal harmful tariffs that raise prices

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will invest in law enforcement and fire departments and fight for more resources for local first responders.
positions.quote: I’ll invest in law enforcement, fire departments, and prevention strategies that strengthen safety while building trust in our communities.

candidates.name: Thomas McMasters

summary.text: Thomas McMasters is the Libertarian Party nominee for Ohio's 10th Congressional District. He is a U.S. Air Force veteran who has worked as a senior consultant.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1989 to 2009.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the State University of New York, Buffalo (1989) and a graduate degree from The Citadel (1997).

priorities.text: Describes himself as anti-war while advocating for a strong military.
priorities.quote: I am anti-war while also advocating for a strong military.

priorities.text: Lists military spending and readiness, and efficiency and value for tax dollars, as the policy areas he is most passionate about.
priorities.quote: Military spending and readiness.  Efficiency and value for our tax dollars.

priorities.text: Supports removing party affiliation from the ballot.
priorities.quote: I believe that eliminating party affiliation on the ballot would be helpful.

statements.quote: We don't need ICE going to swearing in ceremonies to deport people that have legitimately made it that far into the citizenship process.
statements.context: In his answers to the League of Women Voters questions, posted on his campaign website Aug. 23, 2026

statements.quote: We aren't going to get rid of fossil fuel-based power, but we can't be antagonist to green energy either.
statements.context: In his answers to the League of Women Voters questions, posted on his campaign website Aug. 23, 2026

statements.quote: This is a bad idea.  Higher income tax rates make much better sense.
statements.context: On his campaign website, in a Feb. 5, 2019 post about Sen. Elizabeth Warren's proposed wealth tax

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his own campaign website (answers to the League of Women Voters questions, 2026; one 2019 post). No stated position found that directly takes a side on the guide's issue statements, so only statements are shown. His tommcmasters.org site blocked automated access and was not used.

researchNotes: None of the three candidates has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no campaign-website statement of issues was available via Ballotpedia for this race, so priorities and positions are omitted rather than inferred. No independent website was found for Knickerbocker or McMasters. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Turner are added separately.
